newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power slip on slack utility demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power slip on slack utility demand.

text.p: Spot power prices in the most of the U.S. West lost ground Thursday due to a lack of buying interest from utilities, trade sources said.
"A lot of marketers are long, but no utilities are buying," said one trader.

He noted that recent high natural gas prices led many utilities to hold off from selling forward. "They wanted to run as little gas as possible and to max-out their coal, nuclear, and hydro resources."
Next-day Palo Verde firm, peak power was last trading near $23.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from $24.00-25.00 on Wednesday. Firm, off-peak Palo Verde was quoted near $13.25.
Northwest prices, however, were said to find support from the Bonneville Power Administration's decision to raise next-day offers by $1.50 to $2.00 per MWh for Friday.
Next-day California-Oregon border firm, on-peak power was last quoted $25.00-26.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), unchanged from Wednesday. Off-peak COB was quoted near $18.50.
Mid-Columbia firm, peak was quoted $23.50-24.00, down from $25.00-26.00 on Wednesday, as some Northwest utilities sought to undercut Bonneville's offers.
Cash COB for December was quoted $25.40-25.80, compared with $23.00-$23.50 on Wednesday.
Palo Verde for December was quoted $24.00-24.50, up from $21.75-$22.25.
